findings.description: Nothing executed asserts that the documented ledger and the enforced floor name the same frozen node. `tools/g25_audit.py:53-54` resolves the baseline root through `graph['roots'][expression]`, while `tools/red_team_dataplane.py:258,329` resolves it through `contracts/typescript.json` `schemas.roots`; `tools/generate_models.py:926-931` builds graph roots with `roots.setdefault(name, ref)` for module roots but then lets `exports` overwrite the same key, so the two maps are not identical by construction for an aliased name. `test_each_existing_operation_has_an_explicit_mode_switch` compares the wrapper only against `response_baselines`, never against the audit row that generates docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md and comparison.json. I spot-verified one operation by hand (create_job → wrapper response `s011119` = `JobResponseSchema` = audit `baselineRoot`), and a divergence would most likely surface indirectly because tools/g25-oracle.mts:223-234 imports the real exported Zod schema by name, but the documented-versus-enforced link is currently unasserted.
findings.required_fix: Add a test that loads contracts/compatibility/g25/audit.json and crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/schema_graph.json and asserts, for all 36 paired operations, that the committed `<op>:response` root is a `ZodResponseCompatibility` node whose `response` child equals the audit row's `baselineRoot` (and whose `request` child equals the `:strict-response` root), so ledger and floor cannot diverge silently.

limitations: Read-only review with Read/Glob/Grep only. I verified recorded commands, exit codes, durations, toolchain provenance and cargo/unittest stdout inside the check artifacts and read the committed corpora, but I executed no cargo, Node, Zod, AJV or Python, and I could not recompute the reviewed tree hash 4f814fd7… or the checks hash 895b76cb… myself.

Without git access I could not diff against the pre-change tree. That `tools/test_model_fixtures.py:25-31`'s pinned request-side digest (`d9c02bbc…`) is the original pre-change value, and that the only policy-relevant source deltas since attempt-03 are the five fixes I verified, rests on reading the current code plus the attempt-03 finding texts, not on a diff.

contracts/compatibility/g25/{cases,outcomes}.json and crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/schema_graph.json are single-line artifacts, so ripgrep counting is line-based. The 15,658 case/outcome totals, 46 roots, 36 wrappers and the residual-strictness breakdown come from the recorded tool stdout and the generated report (themselves digest-bound to the committed bytes) plus targeted single-pattern greps; I did not enumerate per-case outcomes or count wrapper nodes exhaustively.

Scored chunk `validation-policy` only (validation.rs and its tests, red_team_dataplane.py selection, both oracles, G25_COMPATIBILITY.md, test_g25_generation.py). I did not score the typed-projection decoder internals or the review/CI governance tooling beyond where they supply this chunk's evidence; the stale top-level docs/checks/phase-19-rust-1.99.0-all.json (rustInputsSha256 ebd5fa25…) is governance-chunk scope and I did not re-report it. Phase-20 scope (minimal/default qualification, package/export probes, registry, tag, terminal 49-job CI) was not assessed.

The response expectations are hand-mirrored from the Rust policy in four places (tools/g25-oracle.mts:94-107, tools/schema-oracle.mts:231, tools/make-red-team-fixtures.mjs, and the format list in tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:291-292). The mirrors are engine-independent, self-describing in the byte-compared artifact and empirically cross-checked by the Rust-versus-oracle comparison, but they are not derived from the Rust source, so a shared misreading of the policy would not be caught by the corpora alone.

The mutation corpus traverses the strict vendor response trees, so paths existing only in the frozen TypeScript baseline receive no mutation cases; TypeScript-only constraints are exercised only through base witnesses (whose acceptance I confirmed indirectly from the residual-strictness breakdown containing no `base` case).
